response.text:
No exact precedent for independently tuned positional-versus-item dropout was established by this search; nearby methods separate position modeling or regularize embedding identities. Original [SASRec (ICDM 2018)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.09781) applies dropout after adding item and positional embeddings. Its controlled Table IV ablation reports Beauty NDCG@10 of 0.3142 normally, 0.3183 without positional embeddings, and 0.2436 without dropout. Removing positions hurts Games, Steam and ML-1M; removing dropout hurts all four. These experiments support testing ordinary dropout and position removal, but do not isolate positional versus item dropout.

[SSE-PT (RecSys 2020), with detailed preprint ablations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.05435), separately controls stochastic replacement of user, input-item and output-item embeddings—not positional contributions. On ML-1M, holding the listed architecture and user replacement probability fixed, replacing both input/output item embeddings gives NDCG@10 0.6174, versus 0.6101 for input-only and 0.6164 for output-only. Its regularization comparison reports NDCG@5 0.5293 for L2 plus dropout versus 0.5870 when SSE is added. These results concern a personalized architecture and cannot establish gains from positional dropout.

[AC-TSR (CIKM 2023)](https://www.atailab.cn/seminar2023Fall/pdf/2023_CIKM_Attention%20Calibration%20for%20Transformer-based%20Sequential%20Recommendation.pdf) separates order/distance calibration from item-driven attention. With SASRec fixed as backbone, Sports/Toys Recall@20 is 0.0760/0.1100 for absolute positions, 0.0775/0.1170 without positions, 0.0769/0.1153 for decoupled positions, and 0.0785/0.1193 for its spatial calibrator. This supports prioritizing simple position ablations. Independent dropout remains a plausible distinct implementation, but novelty is unproven; compare joint, item-only, position-only and independent dropout under identical validation, seeds and tuning budgets. Published scores do not predict RecHarness gains.
